# Date header filters echo the previous day west of UTC

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context
Found while reviewing #21220 for #21168. The example exposes an existing Date-header write/projection mismatch; it is not a cell-renderer formatting bug. Promoted by triage from the recorded defect observation so its ownership survives the example's repair.

## The Problem
With a model field typed Date and a DateContainer inline header field, under America/Los_Angeles:

1. Enter calendar day 2026-03-01.
2. The header writer stores the predicate value as 2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z.
3. Shared source projection echoes that Date back into the field.
4. The field's public value becomes 2026-02-28, while the predicate still holds March 1. A UTC-rendered row still says Mar 1, 2026.

The named probe used real DateContainer/DateField modules and exact header writer/HeaderFilter methods at 789492ea6fb423992f21a98bb8f0371de4b6d357, with a controlled Store boundary. This is component/method-runtime evidence, not a browser-matrix result. The existing example's Date test checks the 27-row count and therefore misses the changed displayed day.

## The Architectural Reality
- src/grid/header/Button.mjs:569–570 and its table counterpart turn a Date-field input into new Date(value).
- src/plugin/HeaderFilter.mjs:108–121 projects the exact header-inline contribution with field events suspended.
- DateContainer uses NumberContainer's child projection into DateField.
- src/form/field/Date.mjs:175–178 converts a Date to its local calendar day.
- Design authority: HeaderFilter#syncField JSDoc, “Echoes only the exact inline contribution, suppressing field events that could write it back.” The same day just accepted from the field must survive that write/echo round trip without changing the predicate.
- Closed issue19720/PR19724 concerns value-menu labels. Its UTC-midnight label rule is useful prior art; this ticket concerns the editable inline field.

## The Fix
Resolve the calendar-day representation mismatch at the existing inline writer/shared projection boundary for grid and table. Preserve the chosen day through source echo without changing the stored typed predicate during observation. Keep DateField's unrelated application semantics and cell renderers outside the repair.

## Contract Ledger
| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Date inline input | Existing header writer | A chosen day remains the same after echo | Existing empty/null behavior | Owning JSDoc | UTC and negative-offset round trips |
| Source projection | HeaderFilter#syncField | Predicate epoch/operator/owner stay unchanged; zero feedback writes | Current missing-contribution reset | Owning JSDoc | Source snapshots and writer counter |
| Grid/table parity | Shared projection, native DateContainer | Same result on both headers | Existing non-Date paths | Existing filter docs if wording changes | Both rendered header cases |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Entering 2026-03-01 in a Date inline filter leaves that calendar day in the field after source projection in UTC and America/Los_Angeles.
- [ ] Both Grid and Table satisfy the round trip; the typed Date predicate's epoch, operator and ownership remain unchanged by observation.
- [ ] Clearing the contribution clears the field; existing numeric/text/Boolean projection and no-echo controls still pass.
- [ ] A regression under the owning HeaderFilter unit spec and/or HeaderInlineProjectionNL browser spec asserts the field value as well as the source value/count, in a negative-offset timezone. It fails before the repair and passes afterwards.

## Out of Scope
Cell renderers, header value-menu labels, a new timezone/configuration API, changing generic Record Date parsing, and the filtering example's presentation.

## Avoided Traps
Checking only the matched-row count: it stays correct while the field shows another day. Changing a renderer cannot repair the input/source mismatch.
